bits/e38b35f:
The research said it plainly: cables are spaghetti even for pros
(TouchDesigner's own forum; the ARP 2500 swapped cords for a switch
matrix in 1970), and the touch-native pattern that works is the
modulation matrix with one-tap bindings. So BITS wires are taps, not
cords: select a puppet on the rail and cycle each binding off, gentle,
wild.

Sources are deterministic on purpose: a constant, the voice track's
openness, or beat impulses decaying from the onset grid. Targets:
bounce (scale), shake (seeded jitter), lean (wobble), and stage
trails, the TouchDesigner feedback loop done with a fading wipe so
flung puppets streak. Because every signal derives from the recorded
bit, wired shows replay and render exactly like the preview. WIRE
events toggle latest-wins per (puppet, source, target); 36 unit tests
and the e2e fixture (wired hero, trailing stage) stay green.
